lessons.title: Father’s Heart
lessons.body:
Look Back: In the Gospel of Salvation lesson, we learned how to be saved, our new identity that
results from salvation, and the Great Commission. What was the best part of that lesson to you?
Look Up: In today's lesson, we will learn how to share God’s vision for His Kingdom so that
Christians will desire to become a part of it.
The Father’s Heart is a glimpse into our Heavenly Father’s loving desire. The purpose of the
Father’s Heart is to cast vision and create urgency for expanding the Kingdom of God. By drawing this
illustration, you can help people clearly understand God’s
vision for His Kingdom and see what they need to do in
obedience to Him. The entire presentation should take no
longer than 5 minutes. Draw the Father’s Heart diagram
as you explain it. Use the Fathers Heart to cast vision to
other believers. When you teach the Father’s Heart you
are trying to motivate believers to do three things: spread
the gospel, start/join a Bible Group in their housing
area, and learn 4-Fields from you.

Father’s Heart: [Write Father’s Heart and draw a heart underneath
it.] Then explain: We know that the Father’s Heart is for His Kingdom to
come, and that this is achieved by spreading the gospel until there’s
NoPlaceLeft that hasn’t heard about Jesus.
Kingdom Come: [Write inside the heart KINGDOM COME, and
NoPlaceLeft and Matthew 6:10.] Then explain: We know this by looking at
Matthew 6:10. Jesus instructs His disciples to pray for His Kingdom to
come. Here Jesus prays for the Kingdom of heaven to come down and be on
earth.
Segments: [Write SEGMENTS and Matthew 13:31-32 and draw a
dot.] Then explain: This is a huge global vision that Jesus is sharing. God
wants the gospel to reach every segment of the population on earth. The
word “segments” mean different races, ages, and social groups. In Matthew
13:31-32, Jesus teaches that the Kingdom of God is like a tiny mustard seed
(the dot) that grows into such a large tree that birds can make their nests in
its branches.
[Add circles to the Dot at the bottom of the heart.] Then explain: It starts out very small with few
people, like Jesus’ ministry started with only the 12 disciples, but as it grows it begins to cover all of the

different segments of the earth’s population. We want to see our groups
grow to reach all of the various segments in our society.
4G+ Streams: [Write 4G+ STREAMS and 2Timothy 2:2]. Then
explain: In order for us to achieve saturation – NoPlaceLeft – we need to
see movement. [Add more circles to the dot drawing.] Then explain: In
order to achieve movement we need to follow what Paul told Timothy in
2Timothy 2:2, “What you heard from me, ..teach to faithful men, who will
teach others also.” This is how to achieve four generations (Paul, Timothy,
Faithful Men, Others). This is what we call 4G+ Streams.
Abide: [Draw a Heart-Stick Man and John 15.] Then explain: In
order to do this we must abide in the Word of God. Jesus says that we
cannot do anything apart from Him. For this reason, we need to spend
quality time learning to obey the Word of God every day.
Pray: [Draw Praying-Stick Man and Luke 10:2.] Then explain: We
also need to be people of prayer. Jesus said that we should pray for God to
send out workers into the harvest. Therefore, we have to spend time in
prayer for the workers He is sending out and for the harvest to be reaped.
Conclude the Father’s Heart presentation by asking the people you
are showing it to if they will join you to help achieve the Father’s Heart. As
people say yes, confirm their commitment with a handshake and set a time
when they can join together for Bible study and to pray for the harvest.
lessons.look_forward:
Pray — Ask God to help you understand His heart and feel His desire.
Memorize — Draw Father’s Heart on a sheet of paper.
G.O.A.L. — Share the Father’s Heart with someone else.

lessons.title: S.W.A.P.
lessons.body:
Look Back: In Lesson 1, we learned how to cast vision by sharing the Father’s Heart. We
also set a goal for last week. Describe your experience completing last week’s GOAL.
Look Up: In today's lesson, we will learn how to surrender to God’s plans and abide in
His presence through prayer and Bible study.
You should start each day asking yourself, “Am I full of the Spirit
today?” Are you controlling your thinking and acting, or is the Holy Spirit?
You can stay full of the Spirit by learning the Word of God and doing it from
your heart. Your goal is to have the Holy Spirit guiding you and nothing
else. So, how do you get full of the Spirit, and stay walking in the Spirit?

S — SURRENDER: Being filled with the Spirit starts
with surrender. Surrender is like signing a
blank contract with God. And then asking God
to fill in the terms of the contract as you go about
your day. God wants you to completely surrender to
His WILL. Give yourself completely to God and ask
Him to change your schedule however He wants.
Then, go through your day looking and listening for
Him to guide you to serve Him.

W — WAIT IN PRAYER: You should spend long periods of time in private prayer and
Bible study so that you are spending quality time with God. Being filled involves
waiting to let God act upon you. This takes rooting yourself out. There are times
when you should fast and seek God, anywhere from 1 to 3 days. These are times
when God has to do a deeper work in you, for you to be completely full. You must go to the
WORD seeking directions while signing the blank contract with God every day.

A — AVOID EVEN A HINT OF SIN: Stop letting your sins build up until you confess them
daily or weekly. Instead, develop the discipline of confessing your sins to God when
you do them. Practice examining yourself to find roots of sin that may result in sinful
actions. Ask the Lord, “Shine your light in my life. Show me the dark spots in my heart
that I don’t know about.” Make a covenant with your eyes not to linger upon lustful things.
Make a decision to actively monitor your thoughts, words, and actions, and change them so they
are pleasing to God.

P — PROMPTING: When the Spirit fills you, He’s going to begin prompting you. You are
going to talk about Him, sing about Him, make Him known, praise Him, and thank Him.
Sometimes He’s going to guide you to a person or place to speak life into others. All of
the promptings of the Spirit are going to look just like what Jesus did in His life. Remember that
you are walking in the Spirit every time you say “Yes” to Him. When the Holy Spirit prompts
you, don’t be afraid. Simply, thank Him and do it! Then your life will be filled with more and
more joy because the Spirit is working in you.
lessons.look_forward:
Pray — Surrender your will to do God’s will, whatever it is and whatever it costs.
Memorize — Practice explaining S.W.A.P.
G.O.A.L. — Share the S.W.A.P. lesson with someone else.

lessons.title: 5-Part Strategy / 4-Fields Tools
lessons.body:
Look Back: In Lesson 2, we learned S.W.A.P. We also set a goal for last week.
Describe your experience completing last week’s GOAL.
Look Up: In today's lesson, we will practice drawing the 5-Part Strategy / 4-Fields Tools.

TEACH THE 5-PART STRATEGY / 4-FIELDS TOOLS:
First, draw the structure like you see in this first
picture. Label the heading and enumerate it 1-5, then
draw the 4-Fields lines separating each field with a circle
in the middle. But do not fill in any of the information.
Now that you have created a worksheet, you are ready to
begin teaching.
Once you are skilled at teaching this diagram, you
should be able to give a summary of it within 15-
minutes. With practice, you will learn how much time to
spend explaining each part and you will develop your
own style. When you are about to teach the diagram you
can introduce it by saying: “I am going to show you how
thousands of missionaries around the world are
spreading the gospel, making disciples, and planting
churches to fulfill the Great Commission.”

1. Next, in the heading you should write Entry Strategy
and House of Peace Map. Then go down to Field 1
and fill it in while you explain it.
✓ As you draw it explain: “In Luke 10:1-12, Christ
instructs us to Pray, then Go into the harvest
Sharing the gospel with everyone until we find a
Person of Peace. Then we Network through that
person’s circle of influence inviting all their
family and friends to come learn about Jesus.
This gathering becomes a House of Peace.
2. Next, in the heading you should write Gospel
Strategy and 3-Circles, Stories of Hope. Then, go
back down to Field 2 and fill it in while you explain
it.
✓ As you draw it explain: “In 2 Corinthians 5:17-
21, God tells us that He wants to reconcile the
world back to Himself through Christ and that we
are ambassadors for Christ who have the
responsibility to share the gospel with sinners.
Our first gospel tool is called 3-Circles. This is a
simple illustration showing how sin separated us
from God and how Christ came to redeem us.
When you go out sharing the gospel you will get
four responses:
A. Red Light: When someone responds to the
gospel with hostility, we politely shake the dust off our feet and move on.
B. Yellow Light: This is a Person of Peace. When someone responds to the gospel with
interest, but is not ready to surrender to Christ, we build a relationship with them and
start sharing Stories of Hope. Story of Hope is our second Gospel Strategy tool. As

we share these stories with people, the Word of God gets inside of them and they start
to hope for a new life in Christ. When their hope for Christ becomes stronger than
their desire for sin, they will repent.
C. Green Light: This is a Person of Peace. When someone responds to the gospel with a
willingness to receive Christ as their Lord and Savior then you immediately lead them
in prayer for salvation and start to disciple them.
D. Sometimes, people will respond to the gospel by telling you they are already a
believer. When this happens, you will start to disciple them.
3. Next, in the heading you should write
Discipleship Strategy and 3/3, STD. Then,
go back down to Field 3 and fill it in while
you explain it.
✓ As you draw it explain: In 2 Timothy
3:10-17, God tells us to use Scripture to
train believers how to do good works.
After people receive Christ as Lord, we
begin the discipleship process. Notice
the line separating Field 2 and Field 3
looks like water. This symbolizes the
new believer is getting baptized as soon
as possible. The first tool for achieving
this strategy is called 3/3. This tool is a
simple way to structure our time for the
Bible study group into three parts. For
example, if your group has 90 minutes
you can spend 30 minutes in each part.
A. The first part is called Look Back. In this part you will provide Pastoral Care and
Accountability for everyone to practice the 4-Fields.
B. The second part of your group time is called Look Up. In this part your group looks
up to God for a lesson in the Bible. In this part we use the tool called STD. This is a
Bible study method called Say Teach Do. You will take a single passage of Scripture
to discover what it teaches and how to obey it. The Sword symbolizes the passage of
Scripture. The first thing we do is look to see what the passage has to Say about God,
Sin, Obedience, and Hope. Then, we draw a funnel. The funnel symbolizes that we
summarize all that the passages Says into a sentence with only 15 words. That
sentence is what the passage is Teaching. Last we write a short sentence that says
how to do what the passage teaches.
C. The third part of the Bible study group is called Look Forward. In this last part, we
set a goal for how to obey what we learned. Then we take a few minutes to practice
with each other how to do it so that we will be ready for action. Finally, we cast
vision for what could happen as a result of our obedience to God.

4. Next, in the heading you should write Church Strategy
and Church Circles. Then, go back down to Field 4 and
fill it in while you explain it.
✓ As you draw it explain: “In Acts 2:36-47, we see
the first Spirit-filled church. This is a model for
how God wants us to come together and function as
a community of believers. In this passage of
Scripture, we see the church doing ten important
activities: Leadership, Bible Study, Fellowship,
Baptism, Communion, Worship, Prayer, Giving,
Witnessing, and Discipleship. The dotted circle
represents the community of believers. When the
community commits to help each other grow in
Christ, trace over the dotted line and make it solid
to signify the group has a solid commitment. By
teaching this passage, we intentionally form
believers into a church.
5. Next, in the heading you should write Leadership
Strategy and 4G+, Levels 3-4. Then, go back down to
the middle circle and fill it in while you explain it.
✓ As you draw it, explain: “In 2 Timothy 2:2, we
learn that God wants us to make disciples who
make disciples beyond the 4th generation. Paul, the
1st generation, tells Timothy, the 2nd generation, to
teach faithful men, the 3rd generation, who will
teach others also, 4th generation and beyond. The
tools for building up leaders are called 4G+ and
Levels 3-4 leadership training.”

✓ Conclude the presentation by drawing a big heart
over the entire diagram and declare: “I believe this
represents God’s heart for how He wants us to
bring the world back to Him!”
lessons.look_forward:
Pray — Ask God to give you a vision for how to achieve the Great Commission.
Memorize — Draw Father’s Heart and 5-Part Strategy / 4-Fields Tools on a sheet of paper.
G.O.A.L. — Share the 5-Part Strategy / 4-Fields Tools diagram with someone else.

lessons.title: Entry Strategy – House of Peace Map
lessons.body:
Look Back: In lesson 3, we learned how to share the 5 Part Strategy / 4-Fields Tools. We
also set a goal for last week. Describe your experience completing last week’s GOAL.
Look Up: In today's lesson, we will learn how to
make and use Your House of Peace Map.
The Great Commission is an exciting adventure that
we get to do with Jesus. As a missionary, you must have a
strategy for entering a new community and meeting people.
This is called your Entry Strategy. In Luke 10:1-12, Jesus
explains how the Entry Strategy works.

Before you learn how to do this, you must understand that most people will not accept
you or your message about Jesus. This happens for three main reasons: They do not want to give
up their sinful way of life, They do not trust you, or God is not calling them at that moment.
The good news is that God is at work in the community where you are about to go. He has
already prepared a Person of Peace who will accept you and your message about Jesus. The first
part of your mission is to find the Person of Peace.

You must not try to find a Person of Peace by judging their outward appearance. The
Bible shows that the best Person of Peace is usually the worst sinner. And sometimes the person
who looks like they will accept Christ, turns out to be wolves in sheep’s clothing (Matt 7:15).
The only way you can know if someone’s heart has been prepared by God to receive you and
your message about Jesus, is to share the gospel of salvation with them and see how they
respond.

PERSON OF PEACE SEARCH:
First, I’m going to quickly share a true story in the Bible from John 4:4-42. This story
illustrates the importance of the Person of Peace search.
One day Jesus and His disciples went through a Samaritan village. And Jesus sent His
disciples into town to get some food, while He went to a well and came upon a sinful woman.
She had a bad reputation. She was at the well at a time of the day when she could avoid
other people. So Jesus began talking to her about water. She actually served Him some water.

And then He started talking to her about her sin and her need for Him. Then He presents Himself
as the Savior, the Messiah.
This woman immediately believed in Jesus, and she left her water jars and ran back to
the village. She told the people to come see “the man who told me all I ever did.” And asked,
“Could this be the Christ?”
The Bible says that many people from that town believed because of the woman’s
testimony. And that many more believed because of Jesus’ words.
Here we see a village with a lot of lost people. Out of all those people, Jesus decided to
speak to and to use a sinful woman. She is an example of what we call a Person of Peace.

There are three characteristics that we see in this Samaritan woman- a Person of Peace. A
Person of Peace will:
1. Receive the messenger. She received Jesus, the messenger. He came with the gospel, and
she showed Him hospitality. She had the conversation with Him. She gave Him water.
2. Receive the message. A Person of Peace will receive the message. This woman heard the
gospel, and she responded with faith. That led to change. The Person of Peace is
somebody who hears and responds to the gospel. If you’re going to find the Person of
Peace, you have got to get to the gospel.
3. Receive the mission. This woman took the gospel back to her village. Using her own
testimony, she pointed many from that town to Jesus. They received Him based on this
woman’s testimony.

So a Person of Peace will receive the messenger with hospitality, will receive the
message of the gospel, and will receive the mission. God will use them to bring His message to
that town, or to that village. They are the God-prepared person that God has, and wants to use to
reach that community.

So as we consider your Target Area, and NoPlaceLeft, we need to remember that there
are God-prepared people who are just waiting in the harvest. Although they don’t know that
God values them and wants to use them in His plan, these are people that He wants to use to
reach their community, their friends, their family. And they are just waiting to hear the gospel of
the Kingdom of Jesus Christ.

Before we move on, the Bible has several examples of a Person of Peace. In addition to
The Woman at the Well, in John 4, we will look at seven more examples below. Remember a
Person of Peace meets three characteristics. Examples include the following:
Jesus Showed How To Do It: Disciples Followed Jesus Example:
1. Zachius—Luke 19
2. The Demoniac—Mark 5
3. Levi—Mark 2
4. Woman at well—John 4
5. Cornelius—Acts 10
6. The Jailer—Acts 16
7. Lydia—Acts 16
8. Ethiopian—Acts 8
There are four basic steps to finding a Person of Peace. The tool that you use to achieve
this part of your mission is called House of Peace Map. Look at the following four steps and
practice drawing and explaining it on a piece of paper.
1. In Luke 10:1-2, Jesus commands us to Pray. Notice, He does
not tell us to pray for the harvest. The people in the
community are the harvest. Regardless what we think, Jesus
says the harvest is “great.” The problem is that nobody wants
to labor in the harvest. Therefore, we must pray for the Lord
to send more laborers into the harvest.
• On a sheet of paper write the word Pray and down
below draw a circle with JC/Me in it. The circle
symbolizes Jesus Christ in you. Now draw some dots out to the right. The dots are the
community of people where you are going to find a Person of Peace.
2. In Luke 10:3-4, Jesus commands you to Go into the
community (harvest). He gives a warning that it can be
dangerous. He says not to take anything. The reason is
because God will provide everything you need in the harvest.
He also says not to greet anyone. In other words, He does not
want you to get distracted from the mission.
• Write the word Go and draw an arrow from your
circle into the harvest.
3. In Luke 10:5-8, Jesus commands you to search for a Person
of Peace and build a relationship with them. He instructs you
to say “Peace to this house.” That means, instead of arguing
about religious differences or condemning them, you are to
conduct yourself in a gracious manner so that you are
sharing a message about peace in a peaceful manner. When
you Share the gospel in this manner, if a Person of Peace is
there, then you will make a friend.
• Write the word Share, and at the tip of the arrow, turn one of the dots into a big circle.
Inside the circle write HOP. Congratulations, you found a Person of Peace!

4. In Luke 10:9, Jesus commands you to heal the sick and tell
them about the Kingdom of God. You must believe God
wants to show His love and power by healing them. God
can heal them of various kinds of sickness: physical,
mental, emotional, and spiritual. After God moves in their
life, they will invite everyone they know to come learn
about Jesus. You must be intentional about trying to meet
their entire Network of family and friends. You will become
their teacher and the HOP will become a house church. This
is your House of Peace Map.
• Write the word Network and draw a lot of circles connecting to the HOP. These other
circles are the people coming to learn about God.
YOUR OIKOS:
Now let’s say that you are not going to a new and different community. Instead, you are
going to do missions in and around your own community. In this case, look at yourself as the
Person of Peace who has already experienced the love and power of God. Look at your location as
the House of Peace. Who are all the people in your network?
The Greek word “Oikos” in the Bible means “household”. In biblical times, the word
household included more than just the people who lived together under one roof. Your Oikos
includes your circle of influence, such as family, friends, coworkers, servants, and neighbors,
or relational network (Acts 11:14; 16:31). As ambassadors of Christ, God wants us to show His
love and share the gospel with everyone in our Oikos.

You’re about to learn how to draw and expand your
personal Oikos. We are just considering, “Who are the people
in your life that God wants you to reach out to?” This is the
best place to start making disciples. As a disciple of Christ, the
center of your Oikos is a circle that says JC and Me. The
remainder of your Oikos should focus on the people in your
circle of influence who you are in contact with. These people
may include your family, friends, room-mates, neighbors,
coworkers, etc.
Think about the people you know. Who are some people in your life who claim to be
Christians? Also, who are some of the people in your life who are far from God? In order to put
someone in your Oikos, you should have enough influence with them that you can ask them to
share their opinion on a verse of Scripture with you, and they will. The only kinds of circles in
your Oikos are Disciples and Persons of Peace.

Disciples: A disciple is someone who has surrendered
to Jesus as their personal Lord and Savior. Draw a solid line
from your circle to theirs, write their name in the circle and put
a cross on the circle. Example: I think about my family
member, Josh. And my, neighbor Betty. Also a guy from work,
Todd. As well as a buddy of mine from school, Jason. (Go
ahead and take some time to add some names of people in your
life that claim to be Christians.)

Person Of Peace: A Person of Peace is a man or
woman who is not surrendered to Christ, but who is open and
receptive to the Word of God. The kind of line you draw for
Person of Peace is a dotted line from your circle to theirs.
Write their name in the circle, and do not put a cross on it.
However, when they surrender to Christ, trace over the dotted
line to make it solid and place a cross next to their name.
Example: I think about my family member, Tom. My neighbor
Rick. A guy from work named Kevin. A buddy of mine from
school named Steve. Considering my hobbies, there is a guy named Jon. (Go ahead and take
some time to add some names of people in your life that are far from God.)

Nations: The dots in your Oikos represent the
“nations.” We do not have influence with the dots. The nations
are people from different ethnic groups. Some are already
disciples and some are People of Peace, but some may not be

interested in Jesus at all. When you meet someone and develop a bit of influence with them,
turn the dot into a circle and add them to your Oikos.

Generations: Now open your Bible and read John 17. We see in this chapter that Jesus
was praying for His disciples. Specifically in v.20, He prays for those whom His disciples will
reach. We see here that Jesus prayed for generations. He was
praying for movement. So we want to pray for generations,
starting with the people in our life.
We see from Scripture that Jesus expects us to impact
generations, because He prayed for it. We are able to map out
generations of people with our Oikos. Draw smaller circles
extending from the Disciples and Person of Peace showing that
they have their own circles of influence. Example: I think of
my family member Josh, and his wife Amie who are Christians.
Also my, neighbor Jay and his sister Melissa, who are also
Christians. I also think of my family member, Tom and his
girlfriend Dana who are far from God. Tom’s brother Ray who
is far from God. Ray’s sister, Sara who is far from God. Also, Dana’s brother Robby who is far
from God. And Robby’s buddy Jeff.
You can see from this simple example, we are able to map out many generations of
people who God has placed in our lives. (Go ahead and take some time, and ask the Holy Spirit
to make a map of people in your life, who God wants to reach with His love.)

Prayer Strategy: What we have created here
with our Oikos, is a prayer strategy. This is a Prayer
Map. If you want to see NoPlaceLeft in your Target
Area, you start by seeing NoPlaceLeft in your Oikos.
We should enter into our prayer closets and pray for all
people in three ways:
1. Stir: We pray for God to stir up His Holy Spirit
in disciples. We ask this so they, and us, will
have boldness to share the gospel of Jesus Christ
with unbelievers (Matthew 9:35-39; Luke 6:2).
2. Cultivate: We pray for the people with dotted
lines to their names by asking for God to cultivate the soil of their hearts. We ask this so
the seed of the Gospel will fall on good soil and produce much fruit (Luke 8:4-15).
3. POP: We pray for the dots by asking for God to put us in the path of a Person of Peace
so God can use us to influence them toward Christ (John 6:37,44). Jesus commands his
disciples to seek the “Person of Peace” (Luke 10:5-6).

Will you commit to praying for these people, and looking for opportunities to share the
gospel with them? Pray that God will ignite a movement through the people in your life so that
you can see NoPlaceLeft—starting with your Oikos?
HOP/Oikos: In the following lessons we will use the term HOP/Oikos. This refers to
either your House of Peace Map and/or your personal Oikos. Keep these terms and their
meanings in mind as you study and apply future lessons.

When all the network of people gather at your House of Peace, some of them may not be
saved. Encourage them to join together on a weekly basis to learn more about Jesus. At every
meeting share your Testimony, or 3-Circles and one Story of Hope. As you continue doing this,
many of them will come to faith in Christ over time. You will learn how to do this in Lessons #5,
#6, and #8.
lessons.look_forward:
Pray — Ask God to stir His Spirit inside of you to go out and find a Person of Peace.
Memorize — Draw your House of Peace Map on a sheet of paper.
G.O.A.L. — Go out to find one new Person of Peace to add to your House of Peace Map.

lessons.title: Gospel Strategy – Testimony
lessons.body:
Look Back: In lesson 4, we learned about the House of Peace Map. We also set a goal
for last week. Describe your experience completing last week’s GOAL.
Look Up: In today's lesson, we will learn how to share Your Testimony about what Jesus
has done in your life.
Now we are going help you develop an answer to the question, “What do we say?” We
are going to develop skill using the first tool for sharing your testimony.
TESTIMONY:
We need to know how to tell people
about how Jesus saved our lives. If you don’t
think it’s possible to share your testimony in 2-
minutes, then set your timer and I will just
model it for you.
There was a time in my life when I used to
be an angry alcoholic. But that Lifestyle
destroyed my family and I felt completely hopeless.
One day, I woke up under a bridge. On the ground next to me was a little pamphlet
about Jesus. I read it and learned that even though I was a sinner, God loved me so much
that He sent His Son to die for my sins so I could be forgiven. I believed it and got on my
knees. I prayed for Jesus to become my Lord and Savior
Now that Christ is my Lord and Savior, I love people and have a healthy lifestyle.
Would you like Jesus to become your Lord and Savior and have all your sins forgiven?
Your testimony should be broken into three parts: Far, Broken, and Near. Far describes
your life before you surrendered to Christ. Broken describes your life when you surrendered to
Christ. Near describes your life since you have surrendered to Christ.

Introduction: “There was a time in my life when…”
Far: Consider two words that describe your life before
you chose to follow Jesus. The first word should describe how
you felt. The second word should describe what your lifestyle
was like. For me, it was angry and alcoholic. But you go ahead
and think of your own words that describe your life. I know it
can be hard. Just ask the Holy Spirit to give you two words that
really summarize how your life use to be. Example: “… I used
to be an angry alcoholic.” (Write these two words in the box
on the right, then go ahead and practice it up to this point two
times with your buddy.)

Broken: Now we want to talk about our brokenness and how we came to Jesus. Think of
one word to describe how you felt in your brokenness. This word should describe how terrible
you felt when you finally hit rock bottom before you cried out to God. In your mind, go back to
the moment of your salvation and remember the emotions of
that moment. I like to say that I was hopeless. Example: “But
that Lifestyle destroyed my family and I felt completely
hopeless.” (Write this word in the box on the right, then go
ahead and practice it up to this point two times with your
buddy.)

Heart: The gospel is the heart of your testimony. The
Bible says that the gospel is the power of God. For your
testimony to have the power of God, it must contain the gospel.
No Gospel, no power. The gospel is summarized in two verses Romans 5:8 and 10:9.
Romans 5:8 explains that you believed God loved you and Jesus died for you. Romans
10:9 explains that you responded to what you believed by praying and confessing Christ as
your Lord. Take these two verses and put them in your own words to describe yourself.
Summarize how you came to believe the gospel and how you responded to it. Take some time
and describe the details of that setting. In your mind, go back to the moment of your salvation
and remember the emotions of that moment—let them be expressed on your face and in your
voice. Example: “One day, I woke up under a bridge. On the ground next to me was a little
pamphlet about Jesus. I read it and learned that even though I was a sinner, God loved me so
much that He sent His Son to die for my sins so I could be forgiven. I believed it and got on my
knees. I prayed for Jesus to become my Lord and Savior.” (Once you have got this in your own
words, go ahead and practice up to this point two times with your buddy.)

Near: Now we are going to think of two words that
describe your life now that you are near to and following Jesus.
The first word should describe how good you feel now. The
second word should describe what your lifestyle is like now.
For me, it was love and healthy. Example: “Now that Christ is
my Lord and Savior, I love people and have a healthy
lifestyle.” (Write these two words in the box on the right, then
go ahead and practice up to this point two times.)

Invitation: This is the last part, inviting them into the conversation. The purpose of the
Invitation is to offer salvation. If you do not offer salvation to others then this is not Good News
for anyone else but you. Simply ask, “Would you like Jesus to become your Lord and Savior?…”
If they say yes, lead them in the Prayer For Salvation (Lesson #9).
lessons.look_forward:
Pray — Ask God to help you learn to say your Testimony with the gospel of salvation in it.
Memorize — Spend this week practicing your testimony until you can say it naturally.
G.O.A.L. — Share your testimony with some people in your House of Peace Map.

lessons.title: Gospel Strategy – 3-circles
lessons.body:
Look Back: In lesson 5, we learned how to share our Testimony. We also set a goal for
last week. Describe your experience completing last week’s GOAL.
Look Up: In today's lesson, we will learn how to use 3-Circles to share the gospel.
Now we are going to develop some
skill at using the second tool for what to say,
called the 3-Circles. This is a very powerful
tool for achieving the Gospel Strategy. Now
you will learn how to share your 2-minute
testimony using the 3-Circles. The purpose of
this simple tool is to gain someone’s attention
and present the gospel. By drawing this
illustration, you can help people see clearly
where they are and what they need to do.
After you learn how to draw and explain the 3-
circles, practice blending your own testimony
into it. The entire presentation should take no
longer than 5 minutes. Draw the circles as you explain them. Explain them one at a time, starting
with Broken, then moving to God’s Perfect Design, then finally Jesus.

Broken: [1st draw a broken circle.] Explain: We know that the
world is broken because we can see in the news that crime and war are
all over the world.
[2nd draw crooked lines with the words Money, Sex, and Power.]
Explain: It’s not only the world that is broken. The people are broken. I
tried to deal with the brokenness in my life by chasing after money, sex,
and power. I tried to get as much as I could. But no matter how much I
got, I only became more broken.”

God’s Love: [3rd draw a circle with a heart inside of it.]
Explain: God did not originally plan it this way. God created us
to be in a love relationship with Him.
[4th draw the arrow connecting these two circles.]
Explain: But we turned our back on God and did our own thing.
That is called sin. And sin always leads to brokenness.

Jesus: [5th draw a circle and put a Cross with the two
arrows inside of it.] Explain: But God loves us so much that He
did not want to leave us in our brokenness. God sent His Son
Jesus to come down from heaven. Jesus lived a perfect life and
then died on the cross to pay for all our sins. Then, Jesus rose
from the dead and went back to heaven.

[6th draw the arrow from Broken to Jesus.] Explain: When
we turn our broken lives over to Jesus as our Lord and Savior,
God forgives all our sins and starts to heal our broken lives.

[7th draw an arrow connecting the last two circles.]
Explain: As we follow Jesus, we grow as children of God and
experience the love of God flowing into our lives. Instead of a
broken life, we enjoy God’s purpose and plan for our lives.

Go: [8th draw a dotted line arrow from God’s Love to the
Broken World.] Explain: God loves broken people so much that
He sends us to go back into the broken world to tell them about
Jesus.

After you draw and explain the 3-Circles ask these questions:
1. Have you ever experienced brokenness in your life?
2. Where are you at in this diagram?
3. Where do you want to be?
4. Do you want Jesus to become your Lord and Savior?

In response to the four questions above: If they reject you, the drawing, or try to argue,
then they are not a Person of Peace. Do not press them, politely move on.
In response to the four questions above: If they say they are in the broken circle, but they
are not ready to accept Jesus as their Lord and Savior, they are a yellow light. Build a
relationship with them and start sharing Stories of Hope (Lesson #8).
In response to the four questions above: If they say they are in the broken circle, but they
do want to accept Jesus as their Lord and Savior, then lead them into the Prayer for Salvation
(Lesson #9) and then Affirm them (Lesson #10).
In response to the four questions above: If they say they are already with Jesus, God, or
Going back to help others, then Affirm them (Lesson #10).
lessons.look_forward:
Pray — Ask God to help you learn to show people the 3-Circles.
Memorize — Spend this week practicing the 3-Circles until you can explain it naturally.
G.O.A.L. — Share the 3-Circles with some non-Christians in your House of Peace Map and
with at least one stranger.

lessons.title: Gospel Strategy – Traffic Light
lessons.body:
Look Back: In lesson 6, we learned how to share 3-Circles. We also set a goal for last
week. Describe your experience completing last week’s GOAL.
Look Up: In today's lesson, we will learn about the 4 Types of responses you can expect
from sharing the Gospel with people.
As an ambassador for Christ the most powerful thing God has entrusted to you is the
power of the Gospel. You must learn to wield this power with skill. In this part of your training,
you will have the privilege to go out and share Jesus with potential People of Peace. You must
do two things to find a Person of Peace: pray for God to lead you to one and share your
Testimony and/or 3-Circles with the people you encounter. When someone responds to your
Testimony and/or 3-Circles with desire to receive Christ, your next steps are to lead them in the
Prayer For Salvation (Lesson #9) and then Affirm them (Lesson #10).

GOSPEL RESPONSES:
As we are out, in the community sharing the gospel looking for people of peace, you are
going to encounter four types of responses (Acts 17:32-34). Turn in your Bible to Acts 17:32-34.
(While they’re reading this, draw your stoplight.) We use a traffic light and a cross to illustrate
4 Types of responses.
Alright. What are the different responses that
we see here in this passage, to the gospel? What is
the first one? “Some mocked.” That is a Red-light
response. What was the second response? “We
would like to hear more about this.” That is a
Yellow-light response. And the last one? “They
repented and believed.” That is a Green-light
response.
Let’s go back. The Red-light, whether polite
or rude, represents people who reject the Gospel.
The Yellow-light, “we want to hear more,”
represents People of Peace who are open to hearing
more, but are not ready to surrender to Christ. The Green-light represents people who desire to
surrender to Christ as a result of hearing Your Testimony and/or 3-Circles. In our drawing, the
Cross represents Christians you encounter as you share the gospel with people.
With these 4 Types of responses on your mind, look back at your HOP/Oikos. Everyone
in your HOP/Oikos is going to have one of these four responses. How they respond will define
how you are going to interact with them for the sake of the Kingdom of God. Take a careful look
at the following action-steps.

Now the question is, “What is our response to them?”
Red-Light: When Christ sent His disciples to go find Persons of Peace, He explained that
they would encounter opposition to the gospel (Matthew 10:14; Luke 10:11). When this happens,
we are to move on and keep looking for a Person of Peace, but you may pray for them because
they are included in “praying for all men to come to the knowledge of truth and be saved”
(1Timothy 2:1-8). Do not add red lights to your HOP/Oikos.

Yellow-Light: God is working in many people’s lives drawing them to Christ (John
6:44). Yellow lights are Persons of Peace. They are open and receptive to hearing about God.
When you share your testimony you will find that some people do not reject the gospel, but are
not ready to surrender to Christ as their personal Lord and Savior. Often they will say things
like, “I’m not ready yet, but one day I will be.” Add this Person of Peace to your HOP/Oikos.
When you shared your testimony, the seed of the gospel was planted on the soil of their
heart. Now you are responsible to water that seed by doing Discovery Bible Studies (start by
sharing Stories of Hope in this training manual) with them. We are just getting them into the
Scriptures. As you water that seed, pray for God to give the increase so that they will come to
faith and be saved (1Corinthians 3:6-7).

Green-Light: Sometimes when you share your testimony, people will respond by
expressing desire to receive Christ as their personal Lord and Savior. Immediately pray with
them for their salvation (Lesson #9) and then Affirm them in their new identity (Lesson #10).
After you finish Affirming them, do three things: invite them to attend worship services,
to join the local weekly Bible study, and introduce them to other disciples of Christ. Don’t
forget to add their name to your HOP/Oikos and pray for them regularly.

Cross: When you go out sharing the gospel, some people will respond to you by telling
you that they also believe in Jesus as their Lord and Savior. When you meet them, Affirm them
and invite them to join your training group. Don’t forget to add these believers to your
HOP/Oikos. Try to meet with them on a weekly basis.
lessons.look_forward:
Pray — Ask God to help you learn to tell the difference between Red and Yellow lights.
Memorize — Spend this week practicing your Testimony and 3-Circles.
G.O.A.L. — Ask God to lead you to go find one new Person of Peace. Then go out and share
your Testimony and 3-Circles with at least five strangers.

lessons.title: Gospel Strategy – Stories Of Hope
lessons.body:
Look Back: In lesson 7, we learned how people will respond to the gospel. We also set a
goal for last week. Describe your experience completing last week’s GOAL.
Look Up: In today's lesson, we will learn how to share Stories of Hope that will lead
people to trust Jesus for their salvation.
When you share your Testimony/3-Circles with
someone, you are planting the seed of the gospel
within the soil of their heart. Sometimes they will give
their life to Christ right then and there. If they don’t
give their life to Christ but they are interested in hearing
more about Jesus, then they are a Person of Peace. And,
as you know a Person of Peace is also called a Yellow
Light.

After planting the seed, you are responsible to water it and pray for God to give the
growth. Water the seed by building friendships and sharing stories of hope. Building
friendships is very important because, “nobody cares how much you know, until they know
how much you care.” Love them and water the seed in their hearts.

The Stories of Hope are a selection of stories that Jesus lived and taught. Between the
time of the Crucifixion of Jesus and the writing of the first Gospel account of Christ there was a
period of about 25 years. During this time, followers of Christ advanced the Kingdom of God by
sharing their testimonies and stories about how others came to Christ for the forgiveness of
their sins and eternal life. The Bible is full of these stories. Jesus knew that stories can stir
people’s hearts in ways mere facts do not. Over the ages, disciples have used these stories to
water the seeds of the gospel.

Five of the Stories of Hope are:
1. The Sinful Woman Forgiven. (Luke 7:36-50)
2. The Lost Son. (Luke 15:11-32)
3. The Pharisee and the Tax Collector. (Luke 18:9-17)
4. The Conversion of Zacchaeus. (Luke 19:1-10)
5. The Death, Burial and Resurrection of Jesus. (Luke 22:66-24:12)
When people hear these stories, three important things happen to them: the Word of God
gets inside them, they reflect on the gospel that was sown in their hearts, and they begin to
sympathize with a character in the story. The word sympathy is very important for you to
understand. This means one person can feel what another person is feeling. It is very important
for you to tell the Story of Hope in such a way that the person you are talking to can feel what
it’s like to be the person in the story who is coming to Christ because God wants them to feel
hope in Christ for their salvation.

God causes them to hope for three things: Hope for forgiveness of sins; Hope for a
relationship with God; Hope for a new life in Christ. Hope is extremely powerful. It causes
people to put one foot after the other to move in the direction of what they hope to get.

As you continue to water the seed of the gospel, you will notice changes in them. They
will take steps in the direction of Christ. They may begin asking spiritual questions, praying, and
reading the Bible. Eventually, their hope for Christ will become stronger than their love for sin.
When this happens, they will turn to Christ and surrender to His Lordship over their lives.
Do not try to memorize these stories word for word. You should know them well enough
so that you can tell them in your own words with enthusiasm and emotion. You will be
surprised how easy they are to remember. The better you learn them and practice telling them,
the more effective you will be at grabbing and holding other people’s interest. Make sure you
emphasize the points that correspond to the first three questions below.

After telling the story, ask 5 questions:
1. Which character is most like you?
2. What did this person hope to get from Jesus/God?
3. How did Jesus/God treat this person when they came to Him?
4. How do you think Jesus/God will treat you when you come to Him?
5. Do you want Jesus to become your Lord and Savior now?

Don’t Forget: Every week when the people in your House of Peace join together, share
your Testimony or 3-Circles and then share a new Story of Hope. Continue doing this and by the
time you start the Level 2 Training Manual, you will be able to start a real New Testament
Church!
lessons.look_forward:
Pray — Ask God to help you learn to share Stories of Hope with people.
Memorize — Spend this week practicing a Story of Hope until you can say it naturally.
G.O.A.L. — Share your Testimony or 3-Circles with at least five strangers, and share a Story
of Hope with half of the Yellow Lights in your House of Peace Map.

lessons.title: Gospel Strategy – Prayer For Salvation
lessons.body:
Look Back: In lesson 8, we learned how to share Stories of Hope. We also set a goal for
last week. Describe your experience completing last week’s GOAL.
Look Up: In today’s lesson you will learn how to lead someone in a prayer for salvation.
Some people think it might be wrong to lead another person in prayer for salvation. For this
reason, we will look at a Chapter of the Bible where we see Jesus teaching His disciples how to
pray.
In the first verse of Luke 11, we see that John the Baptist and Jesus both taught their
disciples how to pray: “It happened that while Jesus was praying in a certain place, after He had
finished, one of His disciples said to Him, ‘Lord, teach us to pray just as John also taught his
disciples.’” Jesus gave them a model prayer and then, in the same lesson on prayer, explained
that people can pray to God for the Holy Spirit, which is necessary for salvation.
When someone responds to your Testimony/3-Circles or Story of Hope by saying they
are ready to receive Christ as their Lord and Savior, you should reassure them they made the best
decision of their life. Then grab their hands, tell them to close their eyes, bow their head and
repeat after you. When you lead them in prayer, you must say it in short pieces so that they can
remember what you said and repeat it. There is no one right way to do it. But the following
prayer is very good.
1. Father God,
2. I confess I have sinned.
3. Please forgive me for my sins.
4. I believe Jesus died on the cross for my sins.
5. I believe He rose from the dead.
6. I surrender to Jesus as my Lord and Savior.
7. Please help me change my life.
8. I want to live for You.
9. Thank You for loving me.
10. I pray in Jesus name.
11. Amen.
lessons.look_forward:
Pray — Ask God to help you learn to lead people into a prayer for salvation.
Memorize — Spend this week practicing this Prayer for Salvation.
G.O.A.L. — Share your Testimony or 3-Circles with at least five strangers, and share a Story
of Hope with all the rest of the Yellow Lights in your House of Peace Map.

lessons.title: Gospel Strategy – Affirm
lessons.body:
Look Back: In lesson 9, we learned how to lead someone in a Prayer for Salvation. We
also set a goal for last week. Describe your experience completing last week’s GOAL.
Look Up: In today's lesson, we will learn how to show a Christian what their identity in
Christ actually is. This is a very important step in discipleship because it helps establish a new
believer in the Christian life. This step answers the inner questions that every new believer has:
What just happened to me? What am I now? What am I supposed to do? Who am I now?
Mark Your Bible: Take out your Bible and open it to 2Corinthians 5:17-21. Mark these
words either by underlining them or coloring them:
1. Verse 17, mark the words “new creature.”
2. Verse 18, mark the words “gave us the ministry of reconciliation.”
3. Verse 20, mark the words “ambassadors for Christ.”
AFFIRMATION:
Immediately after you have prayed with them for their salvation, turn to 2Corinthians
5:17-21. As you read the passage, emphasize the words you marked. You should read it in such a
way that they can read it silently as you read it out loud, sitting side by side.
1. Exchange: First, start with verse 21. Explain to them, “In verse 21, we learn that Jesus was
perfectly sinless, but when He hung on the cross, He took our sins upon Himself and gave
His righteousness to us. This exchange is necessary because this is how God punishes sin,
forgives sinners, and reconciles believers to Himself. When you gave your life to Jesus,
this exchange happened between you and Christ.”

2. Identity: Second, point to the words marked in verse 17. Explain to them because of the
exchange, something great happened to them. Ask them, “What are you now?” They should
tell you “I am a new creature.” If they are a little shy, encourage them by saying, “Let me
hear you say ‘I am a new creature!’”

3. Responsibility: Third, point to the words marked in verse 18. Ask them, “What is the
responsibility that God gave to you?” Their answer should be, “The ministry of
reconciliation.” Explain the word reconciliation means two people who were in conflict are
now at peace. Tell them they were in conflict with God, but because they surrendered to
Christ as their Lord, they now have peace with God. Tell them, just like God used me to
bring you to Christ, He will use you to bring others to Christ.

4. Identity: Fourth, point to the words marked in verse 20. Ask them, “Who are you now?”
Their answer should be, “I am an ambassador for Christ.” If they are a little shy, encourage
them by saying, “Let me hear you say ‘I am an ambassador for Christ!’” Explain to them that
an ambassador is someone who represents the Kingdom of Jesus in this world.

BRING:
You have begun the discipleship process. Now you must continue helping the new
believer follow Christ. You should do three things:
1. After you affirm someone, the first thing you should do is introduce them to other followers
of Christ who will help them in their new life. If there are other Christians nearby, make the
introductions right away.

2. After you affirm someone the second thing you should do is invite them to church. Tell them
you will contact them about 30 minutes before church begins and pick them up to go with
you. Then, make sure you follow up with them.

3. After you affirm someone the third thing you should do is invite them to your Bible study
group. Tell them you will contact them about 30 minutes before church begins and pick them
up to go with you. Then, make sure you follow up with them.
lessons.look_forward:
Pray — Ask God to help you learn to Affirm fellow believers in their identity.
Memorize — Spend this week practicing how to do the Affirm.
G.O.A.L. — Share your Testimony or 3-Circles with at least five strangers, and share a Story
of Hope with Yellow Lights in your House of Peace Map. Go to all the Believers in your
House of Peace Map and Affirm them.

levels.name: Church Planter
levels.description: How to form your group of new believers into a healthy church that grows deep and wide.

lessons.title: Baptize Believers
lessons.body:
CHURCH PLANTER: This picture shows one solid dot. It symbolizes the Church God will use to plant. As a Church Planter, you will learn nine essential things you need to become an effective Disciple-maker and pastor for Jesus Christ.

• Baptize Believers • Model like Jesus and Paul • Start a Church

• Serve Communion • How to study Scripture • Grow the Church

• Train believers • Lead Bible studies • Help others grow spiritually

THE CHURCH WHAT IS A NEW TESTAMENT CHURCH? Everything we do must be done in accord with the nature of God, “Therefore, be imitators of God, as beloved children” (Eph 5:1). God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit are three persons yet one God. Father, Son, and Spirit have existed forever together in community as One. This can be traced all the way back to Genesis 1:26 where God refers to Himself as “Us” and “Our.” Also in John 1:1-2, “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was in the beginning with God.” Just as the Father, Son, and Spirit are One, so the children of God are one Body in Christ (1Cor 10:17; 12:12-13). Therefore, Disciples should live in community with God because God created mankind in His own image and likeness.

The necessity for Disciples to live together in community is so important to God that His plan of salvation through Christ calls us together as one body, with Christ as the head. In fact the word “Church” in the original Greek (ekklesia), actually means “assembly.” In the Bible, this word usually refers to an assembly who has gathered in response to a herald who called them out. In reference to Christianity, God sends a herald of the gospel to call people out of the world and into the Kingdom of Christ (Rom 10:13-17). People who respond to the gospel by placing their faith in Christ are the biblical “Church.” The Scriptures also refer to Disciples as God's household. Before Christ ascended to the right hand of the Father, He promised His Disciples that He was going to prepare a place for them in His Father’s house so that we could be together forever (John 14:1-6). Just a few chapters later, Jesus prayed for His Disciples, that we would all be one together with God (John 17:20-24).

Jesus, our perfect example of how to fulfill the will of our heavenly Father, demonstrated with His own life how to live in community and how to build the community of Christ. Our Lord called people to follow Him. Those who accepted His invitation assembled in large crowds to hear the preaching of God's Word. Nevertheless, Jesus made Disciples in small assemblies. As we study the life and work of Christ, we see small groups in almost every chapter of the four gospels. This pattern was so important to Christ and the apostles that they continued the practice of small groups since Pentecost throughout the New Testament. In fact, the words “one another” are found in the New Testament numerous times. Small groups met for fellowship, discipleship, prayer, worship, and missions work. Disciples, missionaries, and Churches continue to meet in small groups all around the world.

In fact, a small group is one of the most effective ways for helping people change their lives. This is because most people who come to Christ have many struggles and need a loving support network to help them overcome their past. As the Father draws people to His Son, we need to receive them with open arms and welcome them to join our small groups. If they are not received with the love of Christ, they will be tempted to go back to their old friends and return to a life of sin. Knowing this, we are responsible to graciously overlook many of their flaws and welcome them to join us in our walk with the Lord (Eph 4:2-3). As we all walk together with Christ those flaws that we all have will be replaced with Christ-like character over time.

Most people think of a Church as a place or building. But it is not a place or a building. The Church is the people who God called out of the world into the Kingdom of Christ. Look carefully at how the Scripture describes the Church: “The Churches of Asia greet you. Aquila and Prisca greet you heartily in the Lord, with the Church that is in their house” (1Cor 16:20). There is a difference between the Universal Church and the Local Church. The Universal Church is made up of all the believers of all times who are in heaven and on earth (Heb 12:22-23). A Local Church is a group of believers who assemble together in order to live in a covenant relationship with each other under the Lordship of Christ. According to Scripture, the smallest size a Church can be is two believers because it takes a minimum of two to form an assembly, and Jesus said wherever two or more are gathered in His name He will be in their midst (Matt 18:20).

There are two primary marks that a group of Disciples must have to become a true Church. For example, when the police look for someone, they usually have a description of what the suspect looks like. It describes marks such as tattoos and scars that distinguish the suspect from other people so they can find the right person. Likewise, the Church you start should have two primary identifying marks. The first mark is the right teaching and learning of God's Word. The second mark is the right practice of baptism and communion. It is this second mark that turns a House of Peace into a local Church. You will learn how to turn your Houses of Peace into true Churches in this training manual.

A Church is organized with a basic leadership structure. Each Church will have at least one pastor, but preferably two or more pastors who are working together. Their responsibility is to help members of the Church trust, love, and obey God. There are three basic functions of the Church: spread the gospel, make Disciples, and worship God. As the Church grows, deacons are selected to assist the pastors. Qualifications for pastors and deacons of mature Churches are found in 1Timothy 3:1-13. Qualifications for leaders of new Churches are found in Titus 1:5-9.

Two things determine if a Church is healthy. First, the difference between a healthy and an unhealthy Church is determined by how sincerely the members are surrendered to Christ as Lord. A healthy Church loves God, loves others, and works to change the world. As the members walk in step with the Spirit they will thrive in at least ten areas: leadership, Bible study, baptism, communion, prayer, worship, witnessing, giving, and discipleship.

The second difference between an unhealthy Church and a healthy Church is procreation. It can be compared to a child. Just as a healthy child should grow up to be fruitful, multiply, and fill the earth, each Church should grow up and give birth to other Churches. This is how God calls us to fulfill the Great Commission. This second difference depends on the first, that Christ is Lord of the Church.

If the local authorities where you are seeking to plant Churches are opposed to calling it a Church, that is ok. Just call it a “small group of believers” or a “Bible study group.” In some parts of the world the Church has to be clandestine. Whatever you call it, God knows what it truly is.
